# scenario G8: exit 4, funding report forced overdrawn (SYNTHETIC)
# argv: --trip-fixture trip_b_europe.json --offline --balance UR=160000 --card Chase Sapphire Preferred --transfer-date 2026-09-15
# exit: 4

TRIP B - Europe multi-city, Jan 15-27 2027
One-way legs, economy, 1 adult on flights / 2 people on hotels. Real cash prices captured by Tsuki on 2026-09-07.
Source: Google Flights + Accor/NH/Hilton, captured 2026-09-07 by Tsuki. Transcribed verbatim.

Wallet (supplied at runtime - nothing is assumed)
  UR: 160,000   valued at 1.00 cents/point
  cards: Chase Sapphire Preferred

Transfer date: 2026-09-15 (ratios and bonuses are looked up on THIS date, not on the travel date - the ratio that applies is the one in force when you transfer)

==============================================================================
FX rates used (table as of 2026-09-08):
  1 EUR = 1.1620 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-07 (4 days old)   [BOOKING-SITE IMPLIED: back-derived from the Novotel Madrid dual-currency quote ($747.81 / EUR643.57 = 
1.1620). One booking page on one date - NOT a market rate.]
  1 GBP = 1.3540 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-08 (3 days old)   [SOURCED on 2026-09-08. Replaces the 1.2700 placeholder, which had no source and understated the London 
hotel by about $42. A sourced rate still goes stale - confirm before trusting.]
  1 CAD = 0.7256 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-08 (3 days old)   [SOURCED on 2026-09-08. Added so the captured CAD 44.60 tax on the real SFO-MAD Aeroplan award can be 
scored instead of carried as an unknown. Confirm before trusting.]
  !! FX RATES REQUIRE CONFIRMATION. EUR is back-derived from a single hotel quote; GBP and CAD were looked up on a date and go stale. Every foreign-currency total below inherits that 
uncertainty.
  !! Supply a rate with --fx GBP=1.36 to take responsibility for it and clear the marker.
==============================================================================

Valuation: cash is scored at 1.00 cents per point ($1.00 cash = 100 points-equivalent). Points and cash are ranked on this single yardstick.

Data problems flagged, NOT silently fixed
  - HOTEL DATES DO NOT LINE UP WITH THE FLIGHTS. Novotel Madrid and NH City Centre Amsterdam are BOTH booked Jan 15-19 2027, which is impossible - you cannot be in two cities on the same 
four nights. The flight legs imply Madrid ~Jan 16-19, Amsterdam Jan 19-23, London Jan 23-27. Reported, NOT corrected: the right dates are a decision for Tsuki, not a guess for the optimizer.
  - Trip A and Trip B both start Jan 15 2027. They appear to be ALTERNATIVES, not one itinerary. Scored separately.
  - Flights are priced for 1 adult, hotels for 2 people. Nothing has been doubled to reconcile this.
  - No London hotel dates were given beyond '4 nights'. Assumed to be the Jan 23-27 window implied by the flights, but the booking dates were not captured.
  - Every Google 'from $X' headline in this capture is LOWER than the cheapest option actually listed beneath it (388 vs 395, 35 vs 44, 450 vs 482). The headline fares were not available in 
the listing; the listed fares are used.

B1 - MRY->MAD, Jan 15 2027, one-way, economy, 1 adult
  Verdict: CASH - Cash is cheaper: $395.00 vs $500.00 on points at 1.0cpp. Do NOT burn points here.
  Cash: $395 British Airways (American, Iberia, Finnair) SFO-MAD, 1 stop LHR 1h45, 5:25pm-5:05pm+1, 14h40
  Points: Air Canada SFO-MAD via YUL (badge 50k pts)
        UR 50,000 -> Air Canada Aeroplan 50,000 @ 1:1 [Chase Sapphire Preferred]
        spend: 50,000 UR
        metal: AC (source: assumed), cabin Y
  Surcharge: $0.00  via Air Canada Aeroplan / metal=* / * / cabin=* / dep=*
        source: project research seed table 2026-09-08 - NOT corroborated against a published source
        PROGRAM POLICY. Asserted for PARTNER awards. Verify before extending to AC's own metal. Government taxes still owed and not modelled here. Applied without a confirmed operating 
carrier because this is a program-wide policy row, which does not depend on the metal.
  Margin: points cost $105.00 MORE than cash (26.6% worse)
  note: Google Flights headline: 'Cheapest from $388'.
  note: The $401 American option's 46k badge maps to American AAdvantage, which is NOT a Chase UR partner.
  note: The $401 Delta option had no points badge and Delta SkyMiles is NOT a Chase UR partner.
  FLAG: Headline said 'from $388' but the cheapest listed option is $395.
  FLAG: NO option actually departs MRY. All four depart SFO or SJC. Monterey positioning is unpriced.
  FLAG: Region classified on SFO-MAD, the route actually priced. The leg is named MRY->MAD but no priced option departs MRY.
  UNVERIFIED: Surcharge note: PROGRAM POLICY. Asserted for PARTNER awards. Verify before extending to AC's own metal. Government taxes still owed and not modelled here. Applied without a 
confirmed operating carrier because this is a program-wide policy row, which does not depend on the metal.
  UNVERIFIED: Points price for Air Canada SFO-MAD via YUL (badge 50k pts) is UNVERIFIED (google_badge_unverified). Google Flights '50k pts' badge. CONFIRMED BY SEATS.AERO 2026-09-08: a real 
SFO-MAD search returned an Aeroplan economy award on 2027-01-15 at exactly 50,000 miles with 9 seats and CAD 44.60 in taxes (tests/fixtures/seats_aero/sfo_mad_real.json). The badge was right
on THIS leg - which is a fact about this leg, not a licence to trust badges generally; the other badges in this trip remain unverified. The real response also shows the operating metal is 
NOT AC alone: it lists AC, LH, UA and VL as possible carriers. Aeroplan's zero surcharge is a program-wide policy and does not depend on the metal, so every one of them resolves to the same 
$0 and the verdict is unaffected. The CAD 44.60 in taxes is NOT included below - CAD has no configured FX rate, so it is an explicit unknown that can only make the points side worse.
  UNVERIFIED: Program attribution for Air Canada SFO-MAD via YUL (badge 50k pts) -> Air Canada Aeroplan is an ASSUMPTION; the source did not name the program.
  UNVERIFIED: British Airways SFO-MAD via LHR (badge 22.5k pts): NOT SCORED - its carrier-imposed surcharge is UNKNOWN (not $0). At 23,000 UR its cost floor is $230.00 before any surcharge, 
against $500.00 for the option chosen above.
  UNVERIFIED: SAME ROUTE, DIFFERENT PROGRAM, NO CARRIER SURCHARGE: Air Canada Aeroplan carries $0 in carrier-imposed surcharge here as a matter of program policy, while British Airways 
Executive Club could not be scored at all because its surcharge on this metal is unknown. Government taxes and airport charges are still owed on both and are not modelled.

departure taxes. United MileagePlus levies no carrier-imposed surcharge as a matter of program policy, so this resolves to a confirmed $0 regardless of metal. GOVERNMENT TAXES AND UK AIR 
PASSENGER DUTY ARE STILL OWED ON THIS LEG AND ARE NOT MODELLED - the $0 covers the carrier surcharge only.
  UNVERIFIED: Program attribution for United LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 27.6k pts) -> United MileagePlus is an ASSUMPTION; the source did not name the program.

bands by distance from London to the DESTINATION COUNTRY'S CAPITAL: Washington DC, 3665 miles. APD is owed on award tickets too and does not care which program or which airline; the captured
CASH fare already contains it, which is why it is added to the points side only. Source: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rates-and-allowances-for-air-passenger-duty. The GBP->USD conversion 
above is marked [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]; this APD figure inherits that uncertainty.

NO leg was scored against live availability. Every points price here is a Google Flights badge, of which exactly one has ever been corroborated. This is not a live margin.

The headline above is a RANGE and must not be quoted as a single number. The spread is carrier-imposed surcharges that are not known. The low end is what the tool can defend today; the high 
end assumes every unknown surcharge turns out to be $0, which is the assumption that turns an unknown into a saving that is not there.

 Residue: what is left in each account afterwards
